text: Man is a result of both his inherited instincts and his education. Among the miners and the seamen, their common occupations and their every-day contact with one another create a feeling of solidarity, while the surrounding dangers maintain courage and pluck. In the cities, on the contrary, the absence of common interest nurtures indifference.
author: Peter Kropotkin
reference: Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution
locator: Chapter VIII, Mutual Aid Amongst Ourselves (continued)
